To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the partition function in the operator algebraic approach is given by a trace of an element in the algebra, (ii) this trace is the same as in the usual approach, (iii) the algebraic approach is based on the existence of an algebra of observables, (iv) this algebra of observables can be realized in a subfactor, (v) the modular invariant partition functions are in one-to-one correspondence with the so-called principal graphs of the subfactor,

the operator algebraic approach to the classification of modular invariant partition functions of statistical mechanics models is a powerful and efficient one, and that this approach is also applicable to the classification of conformal field theories.

(i) The modular invariant partition functions of integrable classical statistical models are given by the partition functions of the corresponding subfactors, which are the simplest examples of conformal field theories; (ii) the subfactor partition functions are given by the characters of the modular invariant partition functions; (iii) the modular invariant partition function is a sum of the characters of the partition function; and (iv) the characters are the partition functions of subfactor models.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(i) the construction of modular invariants in the operator algebraic framework; (ii) the construction of subfactors and their modular invariants; (iii) the relation between modular invariants in conformal field theories and in statistical mechanical models; (iv) the construction of new conformal field theories from known ones by means of subfactor techniques.
